intro: You are a new volunteer at the city zoo. Listen to the volunteer coordinator and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Welcome to the city zoo.
You can grab a map right here.
The penguins are fed every morning at ten o'clock.
The reptile house is kept warm for the snakes and lizards.
This is where keepers prepare the food, so please stay behind the yellow line.
Volunteers get a small discount at the gift shop, so remember to show your badge.
If a visitor feels sick or gets hurt, bring them to the first aid booth right away.

intro: You are a new member at the campus fitness center. Listen to the manager and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Please scan your card here.
The locker rooms are down this hallway.
Treadmills and bikes can be used for thirty minutes.
Always wipe down the benches after you finish your workout.
Yoga and spin classes are held in this studio throughout the week.
You need to complete a short safety session before you can use the climbing wall.
Towels, jump ropes, and resistance bands can be borrowed here, but they must be returned before closing time.

intro: You are a new student at the university library. Listen to the librarian and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Books are checked out here.
These machines let you borrow books yourself.
Recently published titles are displayed on this shelf.
Please keep your voice down on the quiet study floor.
Course reserve materials can only be borrowed for two hours at a time.
You can send documents to these printers from any computer connected to the library network.
When the library is closed, you can drop your books into this slot beside the main door.

intro: You are a new student attending university orientation. Listen to the orientation leader and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Welcome to orientation week, everyone.
Your student ID photo is taken here.
This quad is the center of campus life.
Most of your first-year classes will meet in this building.
Make an appointment with your academic advisor before you register for classes.
Career services can help you write a resume and find a part-time job on campus.
The campus shuttle stops here every fifteen minutes and will take you to the dorms and the downtown area.

intro: You are visiting the science museum with your class. Listen to the museum guide and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Please keep your ticket handy.
Coats and bags can be left here.
This dinosaur skeleton is our most popular exhibit.
In the space exhibit, you can step inside a model rocket.
Children can try simple experiments in this lab with help from our staff.
Short films about the ocean and outer space are shown in the theater every hour.
If you get hungry, the cafeteria on the lower level serves sandwiches, soup, and snacks until four o'clock.

intro: You are a new volunteer at the botanical garden. Listen to the garden guide and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Let's start at the visitor center.
The roses bloom from late spring to fall.
You may touch and smell the herbs here.
The tropical greenhouse is warm and humid all year round.
Turtles and frogs live in this pond, so please don't feed them.
At the seed library, members can borrow seeds and return new ones after harvest.
Before you leave, be sure to visit the garden shop, which sells plants grown right here in our greenhouses.

intro: You are a new student eating at the campus dining hall. Listen to the dining services manager and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Swipe your meal card here.
The salad bar is refilled throughout the day.
Burgers and grilled sandwiches are made to order here.
This station serves meals that are free of nuts, gluten, and dairy.
Machines for water, juice, and iced tea are located along this back wall.
When you finish eating, please place your tray and dishes on this moving belt.
If you want to add more meals to your plan, visit the office next to the exit.

intro: You are a new visitor at the campus art gallery. Listen to the gallery docent and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Welcome to the campus art gallery.
Please don't touch any of the paintings.
These portraits were painted over two hundred years ago.
The sculptures in this courtyard were made by local artists.
Photography is allowed in this wing as long as you turn off your flash.
Students can watch printmakers at work in this studio on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.
The special exhibition changes every season, and this one features landscapes from artists around the world.

intro: You are a new student touring the student union. Listen to the staff member and repeat what you hear.
sentences: This is the student union.
Ask at this desk if you get lost.
The lounge is a great place to relax between classes.
The food court has six restaurants and stays open until midnight.
Most student clubs have offices on this floor, and their doors are usually open.
You can rent pool tables and board games in the game room with your student ID.
Large events like concerts and dances are held in the ballroom, which can hold about five hundred people.

intro: You are a new student in an introductory chemistry course. Listen to the lab safety officer and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Never enter the lab without permission.
Put on your safety goggles before every experiment.
Any chemicals with strong smells must be used under the hood.
If chemicals splash in your eyes, rinse them here for fifteen minutes.
Pull this handle if your clothes catch fire or get covered in chemicals.
The fire extinguisher is beside the door, and every student must learn how to use it.
Never pour chemicals down the sink; instead, place them in the labeled waste containers along the back wall.

intro: You are moving into your dormitory for the first time. Listen to the resident assistant and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Pick up your keys here.
Please use the elevators for heavy boxes.
Each room comes with two beds and two desks.
The washers and dryers in the basement accept your student card.
There's a shared kitchen on every floor, but please clean up after yourself.
The study lounge is open all night, so it's a good spot to prepare for exams.
Please flatten your empty boxes and leave them in the recycling area behind the building by tonight.

intro: You are signing up for the city bike share program. Listen to the program coordinator and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Each station holds about twenty bikes.
Unlock a bike by entering your membership code.
Before riding off, check that both brakes respond smoothly.
You can raise or lower the seat by flipping this lever underneath.
Riders are expected to stay in the marked bike lanes whenever they're available downtown.
Should you notice a flat tire or loose chain, report it before taking the bike.
Make sure the bike clicks firmly into the dock, or you may continue to be charged for the ride.

intro: You are a new volunteer at the aquarium. Listen to the aquarium educator and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Our aquarium houses hundreds of species.
This coral reef tank mimics tropical ocean conditions.
Use two fingers when gently touching the sea stars.
The jellyfish drift in circular tanks designed to keep them from getting injured.
Walking through this tunnel, you'll see sharks gliding just inches above your head.
Through this window, visitors can observe biologists analyzing water samples collected from the bay.
Injured sea turtles are brought to this center, where they're cared for until they're healthy enough to be released.

intro: You are a new student visiting the campus health center. Listen to the nurse and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Please check in at reception first.
Bring your insurance card to every appointment.
Prescriptions can usually be picked up within an hour.
A nurse will take your temperature and blood pressure before the doctor arrives.
Flu shots are offered free of charge to all enrolled students throughout the fall.
Counselors are available for confidential appointments if you're feeling stressed or overwhelmed by coursework.
If you need advice when the center is closed, call the after-hours line printed on your student ID.

intro: You are a music student using the campus recording studio for the first time. Listen to the studio engineer and repeat what you hear.
sentences: This is the main control room.
Engineers adjust every track on this mixing console.
Singers record in the booth to minimize background noise.
Each microphone must be signed out and handled with extreme care.
Guitars and keyboards are stored here, although drums stay set up in the live room.
Always close this heavy door completely, because even a small gap can let outside sound leak in.
Students may reserve the studio for up to three hours per week, provided they've completed the introductory training course.

intro: You are a new member of the campus makerspace. Listen to the technician and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Everyone signs in at this kiosk.
Soldering irons must be switched off after use.
The laser cutter is never left running unattended.
These sewing machines are ideal for costumes, bags, and other fabric projects.
Closed-toe shoes and protective eyewear are required whenever you're working in the woodshop.
Every tool has an outlined spot on this wall, so it's easy to notice what's missing.
Unfinished projects can be stored on these shelves for two weeks, but they must be clearly labeled with your name.

intro: You are a new intern at the history museum. Listen to the curator and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Our tour begins in the rotunda.
These stone tools are thousands of years old.
Early maps reveal how people imagined distant lands.
Light levels here are kept low to protect fragile fabrics from fading.
In the conservation lab, specialists repair damaged artifacts using carefully tested techniques.
Researchers wishing to examine original letters in the archive must request them in advance.
We'll finish on the rooftop terrace, which offers a remarkable view of the oldest neighborhood in the city.

intro: You are a new volunteer at the downtown farmers market. Listen to the market manager and repeat what you hear.
sentences: The market opens at seven sharp.
Most of these vegetables were harvested yesterday.
Ask the cheese vendors before sampling anything on their tables.
The bakery tent usually sells out of bread well before noon.
Local chefs demonstrate seasonal recipes here, and visitors are welcome to taste the results.
Shoppers can exchange their benefit cards for tokens, which are accepted at nearly every stall.
At closing, help vendors collect food scraps so they can be composted rather than sent to a landfill.

intro: You are a new student worker at the campus planetarium. Listen to the director and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Welcome to the campus planetarium.
Our largest meteorite weighs nearly two hundred pounds.
This model shows the planets' relative sizes and distances.
Inside the dome theater, the projector recreates the night sky in remarkable detail.
Once the lights dim, please put away your phones, since screens disrupt the view.
This wall map identifies the constellations that are visible from our latitude during each season.
On clear evenings, the observatory upstairs opens to the public, and volunteers help visitors locate planets through the telescope.

intro: You have just started a part-time job at the campus bookstore. Listen to the manager and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Textbooks are organized by course number.
Used copies are considerably cheaper than new ones.
Renting a textbook can save you over half the cost.
Notebooks, calculators, and lab coats are stocked in this aisle.
At semester's end, we buy back books that remain in good condition.
Before purchasing anything, double-check your syllabus, because professors sometimes switch editions at the last minute.
Feel free to browse in the reading nook, but please return any books you've finished looking at to the cart.

intro: You are an international student who has just arrived at the airport. Listen to the shuttle coordinator and repeat what you hear.
sentences: Follow the signs to ground transportation.
University shuttles depart from this marked zone.
Show your acceptance letter to receive a free ticket.
Large suitcases should be placed in the compartment beneath the bus.
Please board only when the driver confirms that your name appears on the passenger list.
If the shuttle is delayed, you can wait on these benches, which are sheltered from the weather.
The shuttle makes three campus stops, so check this map to find the one nearest your dorm.

intro: You are a new member at the campus recreation center. Listen to the supervisor and repeat what you hear.
sentences: The lap pool reopens after maintenance.
Please run counterclockwise on the indoor track.
Courts can be reserved online up to three days ahead.
Kayaks and tents can be rented here for weekend camping trips.
Staff members in the gear shop can recommend equipment suited to your experience level.
Squash rackets are provided, but you'll need to bring non-marking shoes to protect the floor.
Guided hiking trips are posted on this board, and spaces often fill up within hours of being announced.
